record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: interpretation of the BEC-derived dimension r
record.original_question: What physical interpretation should be assigned to the Bose-Einstein-correlation-derived dimension r if the hadron-mass dependence of r(m), the high inferred hadron-emitter energy densities, and the analogy with Bose condensates suggest that the relevant scale may resemble an inter-particle separation proportional to 1/√mass rather than an ordinary emitter size?

evidence.quote: In trying to gain an insight into the r(m) behaviour and the energy density of the hadron emitter it may be instructive to turn to other phenomena related to the Bose-Einstein statistics.
One of them are the Bose condensates where it was shown [5] that at equal very low temperature their inter-atomic separations are proportional to 1/√matom and not to their dimension.
This comparison coupled to the behaviour of r(m) and the high emitter energy densities may point to the need to re-examine the interpretation given to the BEC derived dimension r.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Bose-Einstein correlations (BEC) among identical hadrons produced in e+e− → hadrons. From a Goldhaber-type or Gaussian fit to the two-particle BEC enhancement near zero relative four-momentum, one extracts a length scale r, conventionally interpreted as the spatial size of the hadron emitter. Empirically, when r is measured separately for pairs of identical hadrons of different species and is plotted as a function of the hadron mass m, the resulting function r(m) decreases with m in a way compatible with r(m) ∝ 1/√m. In addition, naive estimates of the energy density inside the emitter volume of radius r(m) come out anomalously large. By analogy, in a non-relativistic Bose-Einstein condensate of atoms of mass m_atom held at a fixed very low temperature, the mean inter-atomic separation scales as 1/√m_atom and represents an inter-particle distance rather than the size of the trap or cloud.

Problem: Determine the correct physical interpretation of the BEC-derived length scale r in e+e− → hadrons. Specifically, decide whether r(m) should be interpreted as
(a) the spatial extent (radius) of the hadron-emitting source, or
(b) a typical inter-particle separation between identical hadrons in the produced multi-hadron system (analogous to the inter-atomic separation in a Bose condensate),
or some other well-defined geometric/dynamical quantity, in a way that is simultaneously consistent with (i) the observed 1/√m scaling of r(m), (ii) the inferred high energy densities, and (iii) the analogy with Bose-Einstein condensates. Provide a theoretical framework justifying the chosen interpretation.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., MDPI Physics 2019, LHCb/CMS BEC studies, and reviews) still discusses the mass dependence r(m) ∝ 1/√m and offers competing interpretations — including emitter size, inter-particle separation between overlapping hadrons, and uncertainty-principle-based explanations — without a consensus settled interpretation. The question of the correct physical meaning of the BEC-derived r remains under active discussion.

status_evidence.title: The Bose-Einstein Correlations and the Strong Coupling Constant at Low Energies
status_evidence.snippet: R dimension depends on the particle mass and is found to be proportional to 1/√m; the R radius corresponds to the distance r between the centers of two strongly overlapping correlated particles.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative interpretations of r as an inter-particle distance, not an emitter size, continue to be proposed.

status_evidence.title: Bose-Einstein correlations of charged hadrons in pp collisions at 13 TeV (CMS)
status_evidence.snippet: Modern BEC measurements still report effective source radii without unique interpretation of the mass and multiplicity dependence.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of the extracted BEC radius is not uniquely fixed by experiment.

status_evidence.title: Bose–Einstein correlations - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: BEC analyses report a 'radius' parameter whose physical meaning depends on the assumed source model.
status_evidence.claim: The physical interpretation of the BEC parameter r remains model-dependent.
